statement: Most failed runs were not chemistry.

and a 2 mm fillet fixed nine in ten.

info-tall-web.lede: What the field team needs to know about the chip before January
s1-text: Each chip runs sample prep, amplification and readout on a card
the size of a credit card. The numbers below come from 212 bench
runs and 14 field days, and they set the bar for the January trial.
info-tall-web.s2-heading: Five steps from sample to result
s2-text: The operator touches the chip twice: load the sample, then read the
result. Everything between is passive: the chip moves fluid by
info-tall-web.step-1: Collect 20 µL of capillary blood with the integrated lancet
info-tall-web.step-2: Close the lid: the buffer pouch bursts and lyses the sample
info-tall-web.step-3: The chip meters the lysate into the amplification chamber
info-tall-web.step-4: Isothermal heater runs 30 minutes at a steady 65 °C
info-tall-web.step-5: Read the lateral-flow strip, or scan it with the phone app
info-tall-web.s3-heading: Why the channel is shaped this way
info-tall-web.s4-heading: What the January trial will measure
s4-text: Three clinics, six weeks, and one number decides whether the chip
moves on to the regulatory study: how many of the screened patients
end up with an evaluable result on the first attempt.
info-tall-web.s4-caption: Enrolment funnel from screened patients to evaluable results (target numbers).
